newsitem.title: Luxembourg: EU slaps restrictions on Burmese officials.
newsitem.headline: EU slaps restrictions on Burmese officials.

text.p: The European Union on Monday imposed strict limits on contacts with Burmese officials in response to what the bloc sees as the failure of Burma's military government to end human rights abuses.
Diplomats said foreign ministers of the 15-nation bloc agreed new restrictions without discussion as they began a scheduled meeting in Luxembourg.

The new sanctions include a refusal of entry visas to senior members of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) and their families, and to senior members of Burma's military and security forces viewed by the EU as impeding the country's transition to democracy.
High-level EU visits to Burma by ministers and senior officials were also suspended.
In a statement, the ministers said the SLORC had failed "to demonstrate any willingness to respond to the concerns of the United Nations General Assembly and the European Union."
"Further measures may need to be considered," the ministers warned.
The EU has already imposed a number of restrictions on Burma, including an arms embargo and the suspension of non-humanitarian aid and development programmes.

Burma's military government sparked international anger last week when it detained, Kyi Maung, a 75-year-old official in Nobel Peace laureate's Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party.
NLD sources said on Monday that Kyi Maung had now been released. He was held for a suspected role in a student sit-in protest the same day.
